quests.instruction: On the bookshelf, the dictionary sits above the atlas. That means the atlas sits…
quests.hint: Picture the two books stacked, one on top of the other.
quests.explanation: Above means higher up than something. The one underneath it is below.
quests.funFact: On most maps “above” means north, but that’s only because mapmakers agreed to draw them that way.

quests.instruction: Raj pushed his bike up the steep road, puffing hard. On the way back, he coasted…
quests.hint: Picture the ride home: the road tilts the other way and his legs get a rest.
quests.explanation: Uphill means going up a slope, which takes effort. Downhill means going down it, where gravity does the work.
quests.funFact: Gravity pulls a bike down a slope, which is why you can coast without pedaling.

quests.instruction: In our house, the bedrooms are upstairs. The kitchen is on the lower level, so we go ___ for breakfast.
quests.hint: Which way do you walk from your bed to the front door?
quests.explanation: Upstairs is the floor above you, reached by climbing. Downstairs is the floor below.
quests.funFact: The Burj Khalifa has more than 160 floors, so almost everyone takes the lift.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “forward”? (taking three steps ahead vs. taking three steps in reverse)
quests.hint: How does a toy car move when you rewind it?
quests.explanation: Forward means in the direction you face. Backward means the other way, behind you.
quests.funFact: Hummingbirds can fly forward, backward and even hover in one spot.

quests.instruction: Two magnets pull toward each other when the right ends meet. When the wrong ends meet, they push each other…
quests.hint: Try pressing two matching magnet ends together; they refuse.
quests.explanation: Toward means moving closer to something. Away means moving farther from it.
quests.funFact: Earth acts like a giant magnet, which is why a compass needle points north.

quests.instruction: Penguins live in the far south of the world. Polar bears live near the ___ Pole.
quests.hint: Which pole is drawn at the top of a globe?
quests.explanation: North and south are opposite directions on a compass. Polar bears live in the Arctic, in the north, while penguins live in the south.
quests.funFact: Penguins and polar bears never meet in the wild because they live at opposite ends of the Earth.

quests.instruction: The ball sailed over the fence. Our puppy found a gap and squeezed ___ it.
quests.hint: What do digging dogs do to the ground beneath a fence?
quests.explanation: Over means passing above something. Under means passing below it.
quests.funFact: Bridges carry roads over rivers, and tunnels carry them under.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “tall”? (a giraffe reaching for treetop leaves vs. a garden gnome)
quests.hint: Line up the basketball player next to the first-graders.
quests.explanation: Tall means reaching far upward. Short means not very high from bottom to top.
quests.funFact: Giraffes are the tallest animals alive; some grow over five metres high.

quests.instruction: The football pitch is as smooth as a table. The dirt track behind the school is full of rocks and ruts. It’s…
quests.hint: What happens to a bike seat when you ride over a lot of stones?
quests.explanation: Flat ground is even all the way across. Bumpy ground goes up and down in small lumps.
quests.funFact: Speed bumps are built into roads so drivers have to slow down.

quests.instruction: Lia eats fruit, sleeps well and plays outside, so she’s usually healthy. When she catches the flu, she feels…
quests.hint: Why would she need to stay home from school?
quests.explanation: Healthy means your body is working well. Sick means something, like an infection, is making you unwell.
quests.funFact: Washing your hands with soap helps wash away germs that can make people ill.

quests.instruction: The toy robot’s arm snapped off. Dad glued it back on, and now the robot is…
quests.hint: Glue and Dad’s patience turned the robot’s arm from useless to useful again.
quests.explanation: Broken means something has stopped working or come apart. Fixed means someone has mended it so it works again.
quests.funFact: In Japan, an art called kintsugi mends broken pottery with gold.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “crowded”? (a school bus at 8 a.m. with kids standing in the aisle vs. the same bus on a holiday with only three riders)
quests.hint: Where would you find plenty of room to stretch your legs?
quests.explanation: Crowded means too many people in too little space. Spacious means there’s plenty of room.
quests.funFact: A double-decker bus has two floors, so it can fit more passengers on the same street.

quests.instruction: Hasan ate lunch by himself on Monday. On Tuesday, he sat with his friends and they ate…
quests.hint: Count how many people are around the table.
quests.explanation: Alone means by yourself. Together means with other people, sharing the same time or place.
quests.funFact: Wolves live and hunt in family groups called packs.

quests.instruction: Isha’s water bottle was lost for two days. Then her teacher spotted it behind the shelf, and it was…
quests.hint: The lost-property box is where forgotten bottles wait to be claimed.
quests.explanation: Lost means you don’t know where something is. Found means it has turned up again.
quests.funFact: Dogs can track lost things by smell because their noses have hundreds of millions of scent receptors.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “cheap”? (a bag of apples vs. a gold ring in a jeweller’s window)
quests.hint: Which of the two would you need months of saving to buy?
quests.explanation: Cheap things cost very little money. Expensive things cost a lot.
quests.funFact: In some places in the past, people used cowrie shells as money.

quests.instruction: A kettle of water on the stove is boiling. A puddle left out on a snowy night turns to ice because it’s…
quests.hint: Water becomes steam at one temperature and ice at a much lower one. Which is this?
quests.explanation: Boiling is extremely hot, hot enough to make water bubble. Freezing is extremely cold, cold enough to turn water to ice.
quests.funFact: At sea level, water freezes at 0°C and boils at 100°C.

quests.instruction: Mina’s new shoes pinch her toes. Her big brother’s old ones slide around on her feet. They’re…
quests.hint: Picture running in each pair: one stays on, the other flops off.
quests.explanation: Tight means fitting very closely, with no room to spare. Loose means there’s too much room.
quests.funFact: Velcro was inspired by burrs that stuck to a Swiss engineer’s dog.

quests.instruction: Polished silver spoons are shiny. A spoon forgotten outside for months turns…
quests.hint: What do dust and rust do to a bright, mirror-like surface?
quests.explanation: Shiny surfaces reflect light and sparkle. Dull ones look flat and faded.
quests.funFact: Silver turns dark over time because it reacts with sulfur in the air; polishing removes the dark layer.

quests.instruction: At the school assembly, everyone had to stand for the national song. When it ended, the teacher said, “You may now…”
quests.hint: What do you do when your legs get tired?
quests.explanation: Standing means being upright on your feet. Sitting means resting on a seat with your legs bent.
quests.funFact: Horses can doze while standing up.

quests.instruction: The baker pulled the bread from the oven this morning, so it’s fresh. A loaf left uncovered for a week turns…
quests.hint: Squeeze a crusty roll that has been sitting out all week.
quests.explanation: Fresh means just made or newly picked. Stale means it has been around too long and lost its good taste and texture.
quests.funFact: Bread goes stale mainly because its starch hardens, not just because it dries out.

quests.instruction: Before you blow out your birthday candles, you take a deep breath in. We call that…
quests.hint: What is the very first thing you do before blowing as hard as you can?
quests.explanation: To exhale is to push air out; the opposite action, taking air in, is to inhale.
quests.funFact: Breathing in brings oxygen into your body, and breathing out gets rid of carbon dioxide.

quests.instruction: The papery skin of an onion is its outer layer. The juicy white part under it is the ___ layer.
quests.hint: Which part do you reach after peeling the onion?
quests.explanation: Outer describes the part on the outside. Inner describes the part closer to the middle.
quests.funFact: Cutting onions makes people cry because the onion releases a gas that irritates the eyes.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “calm”? (a lake with no ripples vs. the sea during a thunderstorm)
quests.hint: Sailors check the sky before setting out. One of these could sink a boat.
quests.explanation: Calm weather and water are still and peaceful. Stormy weather is wild, with strong wind, rain or waves.
quests.funFact: Sailors long ago called the windless belt near the equator “the doldrums”.

quests.instruction: Grandma’s dal is gentle enough for the toddlers. Uncle’s chili sauce makes everyone reach for water. It’s…
quests.hint: What do you reach for when your tongue is burning?
quests.explanation: Mild food has a gentle taste. Spicy food has a strong, hot taste that makes your mouth tingle.
quests.funFact: Chili peppers get their heat from a chemical called capsaicin.

quests.instruction: Fresh potato chips crunch when you bite them. Leave the bag open overnight and they turn…
quests.hint: What happens to cereal that sits in milk for ages?
quests.explanation: Crispy food snaps and crunches. Soggy food has soaked up moisture and gone soft.
quests.funFact: Chips go soft because they soak up moisture from the air.

quests.instruction: Zoya wore a plain white T-shirt to school. For the wedding, she wore a sparkly dress with ribbons and sequins, which was much more…
quests.hint: Save this outfit for a special party; you wouldn’t wear it to school.
quests.explanation: Plain things have no decoration. Fancy things are dressed up with extra details.
quests.funFact: The word “sequin” comes from an Italian word for an old Venetian gold coin.

quests.instruction: Before the rain, Dad put a tarp over the firewood, so the pile was covered. When the rain stopped, he pulled it off, leaving it…
quests.hint: What can you see once the tarp is gone?
quests.explanation: Covered means something is lying on top of it. Uncovered means that cover has been taken away.
quests.funFact: Firewood burns better when it’s dry.

quests.instruction: Before the trip, Sara will pack her suitcase. When she reaches Grandma’s house, her first job is to ___ it.
quests.hint: What do you do with a suitcase full of clothes once you’ve arrived?
quests.explanation: To pack is to put things into a bag for a trip. To unpack is to take everything out again.
quests.funFact: Suitcases with wheels were invented around 1970.

quests.instruction: You bend your knees to sit on the school-bus seat. To get up and walk off, you ___ them.
quests.hint: Think of your knees when you stand up tall instead of sitting.
quests.explanation: Bending folds a joint into a curve. Straightening opens it back out again.
quests.funFact: Your knee works like a door hinge, mainly swinging in one direction.

quests.instruction: The fishermen set out at sunrise. They come home as the sun is going down, at…
quests.hint: When does the sky glow orange for the second time in the day?
quests.explanation: Sunrise is when the sun first appears over the horizon. Sunset is when it disappears below it at the end of the day.
quests.funFact: Astronauts on the International Space Station see about sixteen sunrises and sunsets every day.
